findings.title: Apply the same scene exclusions to every export and published site

evidence.detail: Reads every scene returned by the host; checks chapter selection only.
Manuscript publishing reads every scene with no inactive/excluded filter.
SDK GetScenesForChapter returns the entire manifest list.
Built-in compilation excludes Inactive and ExcludeFromExport scenes.
Extension export context does not expose the compiled, filtered scene set.

findings.trigger: Mark a scene inactive or excluded from export, then export the chapter using Formats or generate a manuscript website.
findings.impact: Passages the writer deliberately withheld can be included in the shared file. Changing format changes the privacy boundary.
findings.recommendation: Pass a canonical filtered manuscript snapshot to contributed exporters, or expose and consistently enforce the same scene eligibility rules in Formats and Publish. Reuse core compilation decisions.
findings.validation: Create a chapter with public, inactive and export-excluded scenes; assert that built-in export, every Formats export, and Publish contain only the public scene.

findings.title: Escape HTML attributes in published links and cover metadata

evidence.detail: A Markdown URL is interpolated directly into a double-quoted href.
Escape replaces ampersand and angle brackets but leaves quotes.
Cover alt interpolates the same incompletely escaped book title.

findings.trigger: Publish a Codex section containing [reader](https://example.invalid/"onmouseover="window.name=123), or export HTML with a crafted title and a cover.
findings.impact: The generated standalone HTML contains an event-handler attribute. Pasted/imported text can become active browser code when someone opens the shared output.
findings.recommendation: Use context-specific attribute encoding, retain the URL scheme allowlist, and treat link destinations as data. Apply the same encoding to language, cover alt and every other interpolated attribute.
findings.validation: The source-linked probe generated an anchor with literal onmouseover="window.name=123". Add malicious quotes/entity/URL tests and a browser assertion that dispatching mouseover cannot execute supplied code.

findings.title: Remove stale generated pages safely when publishing again

evidence.detail: Writes the new list into the selected folder without tracking or removing prior generated files.

findings.trigger: Generate Everything, then regenerate World into the same folder; similarly remove a sensitive entry or shorten the manuscript.
findings.impact: Old chapter/entry files remain in the folder although the new index no longer links to them. Zipping or uploading that folder can disclose content the writer now intended to omit. A cancelled run also leaves a mixture of versions.
findings.recommendation: Stage a complete generation, maintain a manifest of files this publisher owns, and replace that set only after success. Remove obsolete owned files while preserving unrelated user files.
findings.validation: The probe wrote a manuscript then World-only output; chapter-2.html containing the private ending remained. Test scope reduction, renamed/removed entries, cancellation, and unrelated files.

findings.title: Reserve index and chapter filenames when allocating entity slugs

evidence.detail: The generator reserves index.html and chapter-N.html only implicitly.
Slug uniqueness considers entity names only; used starts empty.

findings.trigger: Publish an entity named Index or Chapter 1 together with manuscript chapters.
findings.impact: Two generated SiteFile records have the same output path. An entity can overwrite the index, or a chapter can overwrite an entity page; links then lead to the wrong content.
findings.recommendation: Allocate all output paths from a single case-insensitive namespace, reserving index.html, robots.txt and chapter filenames before entity slugs.
findings.validation: The probe reproduced duplicate index.html and chapter-1.html paths. Require uniqueness across the complete generated file list.

findings.title: Preserve inline action alternatives and suggestion protection through the host

evidence.detail: Definition returns InsertAfterSelection, despite its comment promising a comment.
RPC projects only Text, Disposition and Error, dropping Alternatives and AsSuggestion.
The editor directly inserts/replaces prose via execCommand.
AI rewrite results also populate Alternatives and AsSuggestion.

findings.trigger: Use Toolkit Synonyms/Define or an AI action that returns several alternatives or asks for a suggested edit.
findings.impact: Only the first result survives. Synonyms and AI rewrites replace prose immediately rather than presenting the promised alternatives/review step; dictionary definitions are inserted into manuscript text.
findings.recommendation: Carry the complete inline result contract through RPC and renderer; honor AsSuggestion, present alternatives, and route definitions to an informational/comment disposition. Preserve undo and the original range.
findings.validation: End-to-end test Toolkit synonyms, dictionary definition, AI rewrite alternatives and cancellation: original prose stays unchanged until the explicit action appropriate to the returned disposition.

findings.title: Read CSV records across quoted line breaks

evidence.detail: Splits input into physical lines before parsing quoted fields.

findings.trigger: Import CSV/TSV exported from a spreadsheet where the text cell contains more than one paragraph.
findings.impact: Only the first physical line becomes scene text; later lines are skipped or misinterpreted as separate rows. The imported manuscript is incomplete even though its source is valid.
findings.recommendation: Parse a record stream with quote state across line boundaries; validate unclosed quotes before creating chapters/scenes and report row-level errors without truncating prose.
findings.validation: The probe imported a two-paragraph quoted cell and kept only First paragraph. Test embedded CRLF/LF, quoted delimiters, escaped quotes, and malformed trailing quotes.

findings.title: Respect the Scrivener manuscript tree instead of scanning every folder

evidence.detail: Visits every Folder descendant globally, filtering only the current folder title.

findings.trigger: Import a binder containing a DraftFolder with text directly beneath it and nested folders inside Research or Trash.
findings.impact: Actual draft text directly under the manuscript root is omitted, while research/trash descendant folders become manuscript chapters. Renamed or localized special folders worsen this.
findings.recommendation: Find the manuscript root by binder type and traverse only that subtree with an explicit chapter/scene mapping. Exclude research/trash by ancestry and type, and report unsupported structures.
findings.validation: A synthetic binder probe imported only Unpublished plan from Research and omitted Actual prose from DraftFolder. Add nested draft, root text, localized folder-name and trash fixtures.

findings.title: Decode RTF code pages and Unicode fallback lengths correctly

evidence.detail: Hex escapes are converted directly to Latin-1 characters.
Unicode handling skips only a literal question-mark fallback.

findings.trigger: Import RTF containing Windows-1252 smart quotes or a valid Unicode escape such as \uc1\u233e.
findings.impact: Common punctuation turns into control characters and accented letters can be duplicated. Other declared code pages can corrupt substantially more of the imported manuscript.
findings.recommendation: Track ansicpg and group-scoped uc fallback lengths; decode byte runs using the declared encoding and skip the specified fallback characters/control escapes. Prefer a maintained parser if its scope fits.
findings.validation: The probe converted CP1252 quotes to U+0093/U+0094 and é to ée. Test CP1252 punctuation, non-Western encodings, uc0/uc1/uc2 and nested groups.

findings.title: Make nested Markdown-folder import complete or explicitly reject omitted content

evidence.detail: Imports root files and one directory level only.
TextFilesIn is non-recursive.

findings.trigger: Import a manuscript folder organized as Act/Chapter/scene.md, or another supported folder whose prose is deeper than one level.
findings.impact: Valid scene files are silently outside the scan. A project containing only deeper files is reported as having no Markdown/text; mixed projects import partially without identifying the missing subtree.
findings.recommendation: Traverse nested directories deterministically with a documented chapter mapping, or detect and list omitted subtrees before import. Validate advertised package formats with real fixtures rather than treating every folder as plain text.
findings.validation: The probe placed a scene under Act One/Chapter One and imported zero scenes. Test depth greater than one, mixed roots and nested folders, ordering, and non-manuscript files.

findings.title: Tie continuity review marks to the entity revision that was reviewed

evidence.detail: Reviewed uses a scene/entity key without the entity fingerprint.
The stored review key is sceneId|entityId only.
MarkReviewed marks every entity in the project, including unchanged/unrelated entries.

findings.trigger: Review a scene after a character change, then change that character again before rebasing. Or later change a different entity after marking the scene read.
findings.impact: The scene stays marked reviewed for facts the writer has never checked. Marking all entity IDs can pre-approve future unrelated changes.
findings.recommendation: Store the reviewed fingerprint per scene/entity, mark only the changed entities actually relevant to the scene, and invalidate review status when any fingerprint changes.
findings.validation: The probe changed an entity from baseline v1 to v3 after marking the scene reviewed; the item still reported Reviewed=true. Test successive edits and multiple linked entities.

findings.title: Enroll new Codex entries in continuity tracking without clearing existing work

evidence.detail: Unknown entity IDs are skipped without recording their first-seen fingerprint.
Automatic rebase happens only when the entire baseline is empty.

findings.trigger: Create a Codex entry after the first continuity baseline, then edit it repeatedly.
findings.impact: The UI counts the entry as tracked, but its changes never create worklist items until the user rebases everything, which also clears existing outstanding review state.
findings.recommendation: Merge first-seen entity fingerprints into the baseline while retaining pending differences and review records for existing entries. Make the tracked count reflect actual persisted coverage.
findings.validation: The probe's newly introduced entry had a changed fingerprint and a scene mention but produced no worklist item. Test add-then-edit without a global rebase.

findings.title: Read real location, item and lore bodies for publishing and continuity

evidence.detail: Location, item and lore entries are created with empty sections regardless of stored content.
The same entity types get empty description/sections in continuity input.
Lightweight non-character projections expose identity/name/type but no rich sections.

findings.trigger: Write substantial location/item/lore sections, generate a World website, or edit those facts after establishing a continuity baseline.
findings.impact: The website claims nothing is written for these entities; Insight cannot detect changes to their bodies. Character/custom-entry handling gives a misleading impression that the whole Codex is covered.
findings.recommendation: Extend the existing read-only entity projection to return normalized details for all built-in types and consume it consistently in Publish and Insight.
findings.validation: Create nonempty examples of every built-in entity type; verify exported sections and continuity changes for content edits, not just renames.

findings.title: Normalize image references against the project before health analysis

evidence.detail: Character image input uses GetCharacterImagePathAsync, which returns an absolute path.
Host resolves the stored image reference to an absolute path before returning it.
GetProjectImagesAsync returns project/book-relative image references.
Normalization only changes separators and trims; it cannot reconcile absolute/relative roots.
No present images suppresses all missing-image reports.

findings.trigger: Run Project Health with an existing character portrait, or remove the last file from the image library.
findings.impact: The same valid portrait is called both missing and unused. Conversely, an empty library suppresses missing-image findings entirely. This makes the health report unreliable for cleanup decisions.
findings.recommendation: Resolve every image reference to one canonical identity using the host's project-aware resolver; include all supported image consumers. Remove the early return for an empty library and keep missing/unused classifications distinct.
findings.validation: The probe reports Missing image plus Unused image for one physical portrait and no Missing image for a referenced file when the library is empty.

findings.title: Terminate render requests after a fatal speech-worker error

evidence.detail: ensure_clone runs before the per-segment exception boundary.
Outer request failure emits error but no terminal done and continues waiting for stdin.
The C# consumer yields any error then continues waiting for another reply.

findings.trigger: Model loading or another request-level operation fails during render, for example when switching back from voice design under memory pressure.
findings.impact: The UI can wait indefinitely: the worker is waiting for the next request while the host is waiting for this request's done message.
findings.recommendation: Give every request exactly one terminal success/failure message. Distinguish segment errors from fatal request errors, stop the C# iterator on fatal failure, and keep the engine state truthful.
findings.validation: The Python mock probe exercised main() with ensure_clone failing and captured only {type:error,error:RuntimeError}. Add a host-channel contract test that remains open after that reply and assert prompt termination.

findings.title: Distinguish installed Python packages from downloaded speech models

evidence.detail: DownloadBytes becomes null when the Python environment is built, without checking checkpoint availability.
Installed/no-download status authorizes automatic engine startup.
snapshot_download is called without local_files_only or a pinned revision.
status preparation ensures both model checkpoints.
MLX uses the same unrestricted checkpoint download.

findings.trigger: Cancel initial preparation after packages install but before all weights arrive, then reopen Narration/restart Novalist. Normal prepared restarts also resolve remote model repositories.
findings.impact: A status/list action can resume a multi-gigabyte transfer without a new Prepare action, contrary to the stated explicit-download behavior. Offline startup can also spend time attempting remote resolution.
findings.recommendation: Track and validate the required checkpoint snapshots separately from the environment recipe. Use an offline local-only load path for auto-start; reserve downloads/updates for explicit preparation and pin model revisions.
findings.validation: Simulate a built venv plus missing/partial model cache; listing engines must not contact the network. Test a fully cached restart with network disabled.

findings.title: Cancel queued speech work between passages

evidence.detail: Cancellation ends host reading but sends no worker cancellation operation.
Old replies are discarded only when a subsequent request reads them.
The worker loops through every requested segment without a cancellation check.
Requests are read synchronously; a new request cannot be observed until current rendering completes.

findings.trigger: Stop narration during a render window, then immediately start elsewhere or design another voice.
findings.impact: The GPU continues rendering abandoned passages; the next operation waits behind them. Scratch clips can remain until the next read, and a new playback can feel unresponsive despite Stop succeeding in the UI.
findings.recommendation: Add request cancellation observable between generated passages, with a single protocol reader/queue and a terminal acknowledgement; or safely restart the worker on cancellation where model reload cost is acceptable.
findings.validation: Use a fake multi-passage model with a barrier: cancel after passage one, assert later passages are not generated and the next request is serviced promptly.

findings.title: Scope sprint word counts to the book and draft where the sprint began

evidence.detail: Sprint subscribes only to SceneSaved, without project/book/draft lifecycle handling.
Every save replaces the count with the current book's total.
Start captures only a number, not a project/book/draft identity.

findings.trigger: Start a sprint in a short book, switch to a longer book or draft while it runs, then save a scene.
findings.impact: The difference between two unrelated manuscript totals is recorded as newly written words. Switching to a smaller manuscript can erase valid session progress.
findings.recommendation: Capture the active project/book/draft identity and define a clear transition policy: stop/save the sprint at a scope change, or track per-scope deltas. Keep scene switches within the same draft supported.
findings.validation: Start at 1,000 words, switch to a 50,000-word book and save without writing; the sprint must not report 49,000 new words.

findings.title: Retire misleading compatibility ranges on native legacy extensions

evidence.detail: Legacy Pen & Paper accepts all hosts from 0.0.1 with no maximum.
Depends on removed native sidebar/content-view contributor interfaces.
Legacy Qwen accepts hosts from 1.15.0 with no maximum.
Depends on native IContentViewContributor and Avalonia CreateView descriptors.

findings.trigger: Manually install an older Pen & Paper or Qwen3 extension package into the current Electron host.
findings.impact: The manifests claim compatibility even though the SDK no longer contains their native content-view contracts. Users face load errors or unavailable views without a truthful version boundary.
findings.recommendation: Record the last verified compatible host range and mark the repositories/releases as legacy; direct speech users to the existing Speech extension. Treat any eventual UI migration as a separate decision.
findings.validation: Static compatibility check confirms IContentViewContributor/ISidebarContributor are absent from the current SDK. Validate manifest rejection against current host and acceptance against the last supported native host.

findings.title: Serialize report severity as the strings the report UI expects

evidence.detail: JSON options camel-case properties but do not convert enums to strings.
CSS highlights only Problem and Warning classes.
The received numeric severity is interpolated directly into the CSS class.

findings.trigger: Open Insight Project Health or a report that uses HealthFinding/Severity.
findings.impact: Problem and warning rows serialize as 0/1/2 and miss the intended severity styling, reducing the visual distinction between broken links and informational notes.
findings.recommendation: Use an explicit stable severity wire value or JsonStringEnumConverter, and keep report CSS/rendering aligned with that contract.
findings.validation: Assert that a serialized Problem finding renders a Problem class and the intended indicator; do not rely on C# enum names inferred by JavaScript.

checks.detail: 365 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped against current source. ExtensionFolder global override prevented local extension deployment. Existing warnings: unused MessagePosted events and SDK-generated unreachable-code warning.
37 tests passed; no model weights, GPU or network needed.

11 adversarial source-linked probes reproduced publishing attribute injection/reserved collisions/stale pages, multiline CSV loss, Scrivener subtree selection, nested Markdown omission, RTF decoding, continuity revisions/new entries, and image-reference classification.
Fatal model-load failure emits an error without done; the actual worker handler was exercised with mocks.

All six gallery IDs correspond to current local extension manifests. Gallery uses shared novalist-extensions release repository; release workflow packages per-ID ZIP/manifest/README assets. No gallery CI validator exists. Remote release availability was not queried.

coverage: Read Formats, Publish, Insight, Toolkit and Speech source, tests, manifests, gallery metadata and release workflows; traced critical behavior into host SDK/RPC/editor contracts.
Legacy Pen & Paper and standalone Qwen3 were inspected read-only for compatibility. They are not current gallery entries; no legacy builds or deep RPG feature audit were performed.
Source-linked C# probe artifacts are isolated under artifacts/audit-2026-10-06/extension-probes; no production source, changelog, installed extension or user project was edited.

No real model download, GPU inference, network dictionary/web capture, packaged extension installation, or desktop visual interaction was performed. Cancellation and automatic-download findings are code-confirmed rather than hardware reproductions.

Publishing raw attribute generation is reproduced; active browser execution should be checked separately. Core exclusion/inline-result findings need end-to-end regression tests across the actual renderer.

Further bounded opportunities found but not promoted to separate findings: preserve emphasis and line breaks in rich exports; localize English report bodies/sprint status; avoid rereading the entire manuscript per board/report request; validate gallery schema/unique IDs in CI; ensure Speech Python tests gate tag releases too.
Release reproducibility/SDK pinning and AI-specific provider behavior are assigned to the parent audit to avoid duplicated findings.
